steps.title: Acute T-cell mediated rejection
steps.body: Rising creatinine, graft tenderness, oliguria. Biopsy shows tubulitis and interstitial inflammation (Banff). First-line: high-dose corticosteroids ± antithymocyte globulin for severe cases.
steps.tip: Always rule out infection, dehydration, and calcineurin inhibitor toxicity first.

steps.title: Antibody-mediated rejection (AMR)
steps.body: Often abrupt rise in Cr with donor-specific antibodies. Biopsy: microvascular inflammation, C4d (protocol-dependent), transplant glomerulopathy.
steps.tip: AMR needs plasma exchange, IVIG, rituximab — nephrology/transplant team early.

steps.title: Calcineurin inhibitor toxicity
steps.body: Tacrolimus/cyclosporine cause vasoconstriction and AKI without rejection. Check trough levels, drug interactions, and biopsy if unclear.
steps.tip: Tacrolimus + azole antifungals = dangerous level spikes.

steps.title: Chronic rejection
steps.body: Slowly progressive proteinuria and declining GFR months to years post-transplant. Limited treatment options — optimize immunosuppression and cardiovascular risk.
steps.tip: Non-adherence is a leading cause of late graft loss — ask directly.
